tape: All 12 screens ran at defaults; csp-wheel returned 20 put setups, 16 of them in the 2026-11-20 expiry.
Chart trend on the 20 CSP names: 7 downtrend, 11 mixed, 2 uptrend. The screen hands you a lot of falling paper.
9 of 20 setups carry wide quotes. Score says A, the bid-ask says maybe.
5 names sit at IV rank under 20 (CIFR, FCEL, WOLF, CRML, UMAC): violent charts paying the least they have all year. IV rank is CBOE 52-week on every row.
No correlation clusters tonight (60-day returns, 0.7 linkage), so every name is its own bet.
The screen's earnings flag reads clear on all 20 rows. TMPro's calendar lists a report inside the Nov 20 expiry for OUST, SMMT and CIFR, so all three are hard passes.

setups.deskNote: Doubled off the spring base, then spent two months building a 10-12 shelf on top of a rising 55 EMA. 10 strike sits on the 17k OI support line, BE 8.85 is 16% down. Firm quote, 599 OI. ADX 8.6: it's ranging, which is what a put seller wants.
setups.whyNot: Strike is 27% above the 60-day low (the August dip). Lose 10 and the 9 line is the last shelf. IV rank 38 (52-week) is middling pay. Nov 20 runs past TMPro's earnings calendar (ends Nov 11): check for a print first.

setups.deskNote: Cleanest uptrend on the sheet: 2 to 6 since January, now resting on the 55 EMA and the 10k OI pin at 5. ATR 3.5% is calm for this list and IV rank 57 (52-week) means you are paid above normal for it. Firm quote, 1085 OI.
setups.whyNot: Delta 0.42 is close to the money for 45 cents. Lower highs since the late-August top and the August gap from 3.7 is unfilled. Nov 20 runs past TMPro's earnings calendar (ends Nov 11): check for a print first.

setups.deskNote: Real uptrend (on the bullish-pullback screen too), pulled back 16% in five days straight into the 9 pin and the 21 EMA. That is the kind of dip a put is built for.
setups.whyNot: Wide quote, 17 contracts traded, ATR 9.6%. Want the quote to tighten and 9 to hold a couple of closes before selling into it.

setups.deskNote: Best cushion on the sheet: 10.5 strike is 2.1 ATRs OTM, BE 9.78 is 18% down, under the 11 and 10.5 OI support lines. Five weeks of 11-13 range.
setups.whyNot: Wide quote and 278 OI at the strike. Lower highs since the 15 top. You may not get out cleanly if the range breaks.
setups.fundOptionsNote: ULTI (income ETF) is running an iron condor here for 10-16: 10.5/11.5 puts and 11.5/12.5 calls. Yield overlay, not a directional read.

setups.deskNote: Slow grinder: higher lows all year, ATR 2.9%, IV rank 52 (52-week). Sitting on the 15k OI 5 pin with 1492 OI at the strike.
setups.whyNot: Zero option volume today and a wide quote. The chart says yes, the tape says nobody is home. Watch for real volume.

setups.deskNote: Sitting on the 39k OI support at 15, which is also the strike. Above the 200 and back over the 21 EMA.
setups.whyNot: Lower highs since July, wide quote and 5 contracts traded. Strike AT support means no cushion before the shelf, only after it.

setups.deskNote: Extended: +159% in 60 days. Pullback plan: let it come into the rising 21 EMA or the 3k OI 25 support and sell below that, not here.
setups.whyNot: Strike is 154% above the 60-day low, ATR 12.6%, OI at the strike is 74. Already down 19% in five days.

setups.deskNote: Two-month range 14-20 above a rising 200. 15 strike sits over the 14.5 and 14 OI supports. Liquid: 2097 contracts traded today.
setups.whyNot: Down 9% today, IV rank 14 (52-week) on a name with a 9.5% ATR. Paid the least it has all year to own the next gap.

setups.deskNote: Best cushion of the firm-quote names: higher lows since August, 15 strike 1.8 ATRs out, BE 13.68 is 20% down.
setups.whyNot: TMPro's earnings calendar lists a report inside the Nov 20 expiry. The screen marked it clear. Hard pass. Biotech on top of it.
